questions.title: Doubly Node Contents
questions.description: What does a doubly linked list node hold?
questions.Option4: The value plus both prev and next references

questions.title: Deletion Advantage
questions.description: Why is deleting a known node easier in a doubly linked list than in a singly linked list?
questions.Option1: Doubly linked lists never need deletion logic
questions.Option2: Deletion is impossible in singly linked lists
questions.Option3: The node itself holds prev, so no separate scan for the predecessor is needed
questions.Option4: Both structures need exactly the same steps

questions.title: Snippet Back Link
questions.description: What does this program print?
questions.codesnippet:
class DNode:
    def __init__(self, val):
        self.val = val
        self.prev = None
        self.next = None
a = DNode(1)
b = DNode(2)
a.next = b
b.prev = a
print(b.prev.val)

questions.title: Circular List Definition
questions.description: What makes a linked list circular?
questions.Option1: The first node's next is None
questions.Option2: The last node's next points back to the first node
questions.Option3: Every node's next points to itself
questions.Option4: The head node stores the list's length

questions.title: Cost of the prev Pointer
questions.description: What does adding prev pointers cost compared with a singly linked list?
questions.Option2: Half the memory of a singly linked list

questions.title: Stopping a Circular Walk
questions.description: When traversing a circular linked list, when do you stop?
questions.Option1: When next becomes None — but that never happens
questions.Option4: When the current node returns to the starting (head) node

questions.title: Snippet Both Directions
questions.description: What does this program print?
questions.codesnippet:
class DNode:
    def __init__(self, val):
        self.prev = self.next = None
        self.val = val
a, b = DNode(1), DNode(2)
a.next, b.prev = b, a
print(a.next.val, b.prev.val)

questions.title: Everyday Use Case
questions.description: Which application is a natural fit for a doubly linked list?
questions.Option2: Binary search over a sorted array
questions.Option3: A browser's back/forward navigation over visited pages
questions.Option4: Reading a file into a tuple

questions.title: Sentinel Node Purpose
questions.description: What is the purpose of a sentinel (dummy) node?
questions.Option1: It stores all of the list's data in one place
questions.Option2: It removes special-case handling for operations at the ends or on an empty list
questions.Option3: It always points to the largest element
questions.Option4: It is a second head used only for sorting

questions.title: Snippet Circular Walk
questions.description: head is the circular list 1 → 2 → 3 → (back to 1). What does this print?
questions.codesnippet:
n = head
out = []
for _ in range(5):
    out.append(n.val)
    n = n.next
print(out)

questions.title: Snippet Doubly Insert
questions.description: b (value 2) is inserted between a (1) and c (3). What does this print?
questions.codesnippet:
class DNode:
    def __init__(self, val):
        self.prev = self.next = None
        self.val = val
a, c = DNode(1), DNode(3)
a.next, c.prev = c, a
b = DNode(2)
b.prev, b.next = a, a.next
a.next.prev = b
a.next = b
print(a.next.val, b.next.val)

questions.title: Snippet Doubly Remove
questions.description: In the doubly linked list 1 <-> 2 <-> 3, n is the middle node (value 2). What does this print?
questions.codesnippet:
n.prev.next = n.next
n.next.prev = n.prev
print(n.prev.next.val, n.next.prev.val)

questions.title: Josephus Structure Choice
questions.description: Why does the Josephus elimination problem suit a circular linked list?
questions.Option1: Because the list must stay sorted by value
questions.Option2: Because a stack pops every k-th element automatically
questions.Option3: Because you can keep stepping around the circle, removing every k-th node until one remains
questions.Option4: Because an array must be re-sorted after each removal

questions.title: Snippet Josephus Survivor
questions.description: Simulating every-2nd-person elimination with this code, who survives? What does this print?
questions.codesnippet:
people = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]
i = 0
while len(people) > 1:
    i = (i + 1) % len(people)
    people.pop(i)
    i %= len(people)
print(people[0])

questions.title: Snippet Backward Walk
questions.description: In the doubly linked list 1 <-> 2 <-> 3, tail is node 3. What does this print?
questions.codesnippet:
out = []
cur = tail
while cur:
    out.append(cur.val)
    cur = cur.prev
print(out)

questions.title: Sentinel in a Circular Doubly List
questions.description: How does a sentinel simplify a circular doubly linked list?
questions.Option1: A single sentinel's next and prev bracket the real nodes, so insert and delete never need empty-list or end-of-list special cases
questions.Option2: A sentinel doubles the memory of every node
questions.Option3: Sentinels store the list's actual data
questions.Option4: Circular lists cannot use a sentinel at all

questions.title: Snippet Circular Count
questions.description: In a circular singly list 2 → 4 → 6 → (back to 2), start is node 6. What does this print?
questions.codesnippet:
count = 1
cur = start.next
while cur is not start:
    count += 1
    cur = cur.next
print(count)

questions.title: Snippet Insert Order Check
questions.description: b (value 2) is inserted between a (1) and c (3). What does this print?
questions.codesnippet:
class DNode:
    def __init__(self, val):
        self.prev = self.next = None
        self.val = val
a, c = DNode(1), DNode(3)
a.next, c.prev = c, a
b = DNode(2)
b.next = a.next
b.prev = a
a.next.prev = b
a.next = b
print(c.prev.val, b.prev.val, b.next.val)

questions.title: Snippet Elimination Order
questions.description: Simulating every-2nd elimination on the circle [1, 2, 3]. What does this print?
questions.codesnippet:
circle = [1, 2, 3]
idx = 0
order = []
while circle:
    idx = (idx + 1) % len(circle)
    order.append(circle.pop(idx))
print(order)

questions.title: Circular Backward Traversal
questions.description: In a circular DOUBLY linked list, when must a backward traversal stop?
questions.Option1: When cur.prev is None — though that never happens for interior nodes in a circle
questions.Option2: After exactly twice the list's length, in every case
questions.Option3: When cur returns to the starting node, because no pointer in the circle is ever None
questions.Option4: Circular doubly linked lists cannot be traversed backwards at all
